```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Hayato 2018 built two exposure-response models from the phase 3 SELECT study of
lenvatinib in radioiodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer (RR-DTC) and
used them together to choose a lower starting dose for a follow-up trial:

* a **tumor-growth-inhibition** model for the RECIST 1.1 sum of target-lesion
  diameters, driven by the lenvatinib AUC computed from the average dose between
  two tumor assessments, and
* a weekly **cumulative-logit** model for dose-altering adverse events, graded
  0 (none), 1 (an adverse event leading to dose interruption) and 2 (an adverse
  event leading to dose reduction or withdrawal), driven by the AUC at the
  highest dose taken that week.

The two models were fitted separately, so the package ships them as two files.
Neither has a PK layer: the individual AUCs came from the published population
PK model of Gupta 2016, which is in the package as `Gupta_2016_lenvatinib`.

* Citation: Hayato S, Shumaker R, Ferry J, Binder T, Dutcus CE, Hussein Z.
  Exposure-response analysis and simulation of lenvatinib safety and efficacy in
  patients with radioiodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer. Cancer
  Chemother Pharmacol. 2018;82(6):971-978.
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00280-018-3687-4>

```{r models}
mod_tumor <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Hayato_2018_lenvatinib_tumor"))
mod_ae <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Hayato_2018_lenvatinib_teae_dosemod"))
mod_pk <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Gupta_2016_lenvatinib"))
```

# Population

SELECT randomised 392 patients with RR-DTC 2:1 to lenvatinib 24 mg once daily or
placebo. The tumor-size analysis used 2373 independent-review assessments from
374 patients (248 lenvatinib, 126 placebo) with a baseline and at least one
post-dose assessment; the adverse-event analysis used 7914 weekly reports over
the first 24 weeks from 391 patients (260 lenvatinib, 131 placebo). Hayato 2018
reports no demographics of its own (they are those of the SELECT publication)
and performed no covariate analysis, so neither model carries a covariate other
than exposure and, for the tumor model, the observed baseline tumor size.

# Source trace

| Item | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Tumor ODE `dy/dt = KG*y - Emax*AVAUC/(AVAUC + EC50*R(t))*y`, `R(t) = exp(lambda*t)` | -- | Methods, "Exposure-response model for efficacy" |
| `kgrow_pop` (KG) | 0.000932 /week | Table 1 |
| `emax_pop` (Emax) | 0.0834 /week | Table 1 |
| `lec50` (EC50) | 2.03 ug*h/mL = 2030 ng*h/mL | Table 1 |
| `lam_pop` (lambda) | 0.170 /week | Table 1 |
| `etakgrow`, `etaemax`, `etalam` (additive IIV) | SD 0.00858, 0.0508, 0.0791 /week | Table 1; additive form from Methods |
| `etalec50` (exponential IIV) | CV 40.5% | Table 1; exponential form from Methods |
| `propSd`, `addSd` | 3.89% CV, 1.74 mm | Table 1 |
| AE model `EFF = Emax*AUC/(EC50 + AUC) + eta`, `A_i = B_i + EFF`, `P(AE >= i) = exp(A_i)/(1 + exp(A_i))` | -- | Methods, "Exposure-response model for safety" |
| Per-grade probabilities `P(AE = 2) = P(AE >= 2)`, `P(AE = 1) = P(AE >= 1) - P(AE >= 2)`, `P(AE = 0) = 1 - P(AE >= 1)` | -- | Methods |
| `logite0` (B1) | -5.64 | Table 2 |
| `logitstep1` (B2 - B1) | -0.830 | Table 2 |
| `emax` (Emax on the logit) | 6.55 | Table 2 |
| `lec50` (EC50) | 2.95 ug*h/mL = 2950 ng*h/mL | Table 2 |
| `etalogite0` (subject sensitivity) | SD 1.06 | Table 2 |
| Dose-reduction ladders | 24-20-14-10; 20-14-10-8; 18-14-10-8; 14-10-8-4 mg, then stop | Online Resource Tables 1 and 2 |

# Exposure

Both models take lenvatinib exposure as the steady-state daily AUC
`AUC_LEN = 1000 * F * dose / (CL/F)` in ng*h/mL, with `CL/F` and the capsule
relative bioavailability `F` from Gupta 2016. The SELECT covariates that act on
`CL/F` in that model are not published in Hayato 2018, so the virtual cohort
below uses the Gupta 2016 reference patient (75 kg, normal albumin and alkaline
phosphatase, no interacting co-medication) with its between-subject variability
on `CL/F` and on `F`. The marketed product is a capsule.

```{r cohort}
pk_ini <- mod_pk$iniDf
pk_est <- setNames(pk_ini$est, pk_ini$name)

n_per_arm <- 200
set.seed(20181)
cohort <- data.frame(
  sid = seq_len(n_per_arm),
  cl = exp(pk_est[["lcl"]] + rnorm(n_per_arm, 0, sqrt(pk_est[["etalcl"]]))),
  fcap = exp(pk_est[["lfcap"]] + rnorm(n_per_arm, 0, sqrt(pk_est[["etalfcap"]]))),
  # Subject sensitivity of the adverse-event model (Table 2, SD 1.06), drawn
  # here rather than by rxSolve so that the same patient keeps the same
  # sensitivity in every week and every regimen.
  eta_ae = rnorm(n_per_arm, 0, 1.06)
)

auc_len <- function(dose_mg, cl, fcap) 1000 * fcap * dose_mg / cl

typical_auc_24 <- auc_len(24, exp(pk_est[["lcl"]]), exp(pk_est[["lfcap"]]))
typical_auc_24
summary(auc_len(24, cohort$cl, cohort$fcap))
```

## PKNCA check of the exposure definition

The closed-form `AUC_LEN` is the steady-state AUC over one 24 h dosing interval.
A typical-value solve of the Gupta 2016 model at 24 mg once daily, read by
PKNCA, confirms it. Gupta 2016 splits each dose between a first-order depot and
a zero-order input into the central compartment, so each daily dose is given to
both (the model's `f()` statements apportion it).

```{r pknca}
n_days <- 28
dose_times <- (seq_len(n_days) - 1) * 24
ev_pk <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = 1, time = dose_times, amt = 24, evid = 1, cmt = "depot", rate = 0),
  data.frame(id = 1, time = dose_times, amt = 24, evid = 1, cmt = "central", rate = -2),
  # Observations over the last dosing interval only (day 28, at steady state).
  data.frame(id = 1, time = seq(648, 672, by = 0.25),
             amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central", rate = 0)
) |>
  distinct() |>
  arrange(time, desc(evid)) |>
  mutate(WT = 75, ALB = 40, ALP = 80, CONMED_CYP3A4_IND = 0,
         CONMED_CYP3A4_INH = 0, DIS_HEALTHY = 0, FORM_CAPSULE = 1,
         treatment = "24 mg QD capsule")

# A single-subject solve returns no id column; add it back for PKNCA.
sim_pk <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_pk), ev_pk, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(id = 1, treatment = "24 mg QD capsule")

conc <- sim_pk |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(time = time - 648) |>
  distinct(id, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_df <- data.frame(id = 1, time = 0, amt = 24, treatment = "24 mg QD capsule")

nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE)
))
nca_res <- as.data.frame(nca$result)
auc_ss_nca <- nca_res$PPORRES[nca_res$PPTESTCD == "auclast"]
c(PKNCA_AUC0_24 = auc_ss_nca, closed_form = typical_auc_24)
stopifnot(abs(auc_ss_nca / typical_auc_24 - 1) < 0.02)
```

# Tumor-growth-inhibition model

## Closed-form check

With a constant exposure `A` the tumor ODE integrates exactly:
`y(t) = y0 * exp(KG*t - Emax*(t - log((A + EC50*exp(lambda*t)) / (A + EC50)) / lambda))`.
The typical-value solve must agree with it to numerical precision, which
verifies the transcription of the ODE, the time base and the EC50 units.

```{r tumor-closed-form}
tum_ini <- setNames(mod_tumor$iniDf$est, mod_tumor$iniDf$name)
tum_closed <- function(t, a, y0) {
  kg <- tum_ini[["kgrow_pop"]]
  em <- tum_ini[["emax_pop"]]
  c50 <- exp(tum_ini[["lec50"]])
  lam <- tum_ini[["lam_pop"]]
  y0 * exp(kg * t - em * (t - log((a + c50 * exp(lam * t)) / (a + c50)) / lam))
}
ev_typ <- data.frame(id = 1, time = seq(0, 24, by = 1), evid = 0, cmt = "tumor",
                     AUC_LEN = typical_auc_24, TUM_SLD = 60)
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_tumor), ev_typ, returnType = "data.frame")
typ$closed <- tum_closed(typ$time, typical_auc_24, 60)
stopifnot(max(abs(typ$tumor / typ$closed - 1)) < 1e-4)
round(100 * typ$tumor[typ$time %in% c(8, 16, 24)] / 60, 1)

# Placebo: with no exposure the tumor grows at KG = 0.000932 /week, i.e. about
# 2% over 24 weeks.
ev_pbo <- mutate(ev_typ, AUC_LEN = 0)
pbo <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_tumor), ev_pbo, returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(abs(pbo$tumor[pbo$time == 24] / (60 * exp(0.000932 * 24)) - 1) < 1e-6)
```

## Between-subject spread at constant 24 mg

Companion to Figure 1 (the visual predictive check, which needs the SELECT data):
the simulated 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles of tumor size for patients held at
24 mg and for placebo, with the combined residual error included.

```{r tumor-vpc}
ev_vpc <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = cohort$sid, arm = "Lenvatinib 24 mg",
             AUC_LEN = auc_len(24, cohort$cl, cohort$fcap)),
  data.frame(id = cohort$sid + n_per_arm, arm = "Placebo", AUC_LEN = 0)
) |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, 24, by = 2)) |>
  mutate(evid = 0, cmt = "tumor", TUM_SLD = 60) |>
  arrange(id, time)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2018)
sim_vpc <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_tumor, ev_vpc, keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame")
sim_vpc |>
  group_by(arm, time) |>
  summarise(p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), p50 = median(sim), p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  labs(x = "Time (weeks)", y = "Sum of target-lesion diameters (mm)",
       title = "Simulated 90% interval, baseline 60 mm (cf. Figure 1 of Hayato 2018)")
```

# Dose-altering adverse-event model

## Closed-form check

The model's weekly probabilities are reproduced from Table 2 by hand. The
check passes each simulated patient's sensitivity `eta` to the packaged model
as a parameter so the same values can be recomputed independently.

```{r ae-closed-form}
# An ordinal endpoint has no sigma, so every solve warns 'No sigma parameters
# in the model'; that one warning is muffled, any other still surfaces.
muffle_no_sigma <- function(w) {
  if (grepl("No sigma parameters", conditionMessage(w))) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
}
ae_probs <- function(auc, eta) {
  d <- data.frame(id = seq_along(auc), time = 0, evid = 0, AUC_LEN = auc)
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_ae), d,
                    params = data.frame(id = seq_along(auc), etalogite0 = eta),
                    returnType = "data.frame"),
    warning = muffle_no_sigma
  )
}

auc_wk1 <- auc_len(24, cohort$cl, cohort$fcap)
wk1 <- ae_probs(auc_wk1, cohort$eta_ae)
by_hand_ge1 <- plogis(-5.64 + 6.55 * auc_wk1 / (2950 + auc_wk1) + cohort$eta_ae)
by_hand_ge2 <- plogis(-5.64 - 0.830 + 6.55 * auc_wk1 / (2950 + auc_wk1) + cohort$eta_ae)
stopifnot(
  max(abs(wk1$prob_teae_dosemod - by_hand_ge1)) < 1e-10,
  max(abs(wk1$prob_teae_dosered - by_hand_ge2)) < 1e-10,
  max(abs(wk1$p0 + wk1$p1 + wk1$p2 - 1)) < 1e-12
)
```

## Week 1 against Figure 2

Figure 2 plots the weekly probability of a dose interruption (panel a) and of a
dose reduction or withdrawal (panel b) among lenvatinib patients. In week 1
every patient takes 24 mg, so the population average of the model's per-patient
probabilities can be compared directly with the median simulated curve, read
from the figure by the maintainers as about 0.073 (a) and 0.085 (b).

```{r ae-week1}
wk1_avg <- c(interruption = mean(wk1$p1), reduction_or_withdrawal = mean(wk1$p2))
round(wk1_avg, 3)
stopifnot(
  abs(wk1_avg[["interruption"]] - 0.073) < 0.02,
  abs(wk1_avg[["reduction_or_withdrawal"]] - 0.085) < 0.02
)
```

# Dosing-regimen simulation

Hayato 2018 simulated 24 weeks of dosing history for seven starting-dose
regimens with the adverse-event model, then drove the tumor model with the
resulting doses. The reduction ladders are those of Online Resource Tables 1
and 2. The paper does not spell out how an interruption or an up-titration is
executed, so the simulation below applies these rules (see Assumptions and
deviations):

* a grade-2 week lowers the dose one step on the current ladder from the next
  week; a reduction beyond the fourth level withdraws the drug;
* a grade-1 week takes the next week off drug, then the same dose resumes;
* with up-titration, a patient who is still on the first level of the current
  ladder and has never had a reduction moves to the next ladder at weeks 5, 9,
  ... (every 4 weeks), up to 24 mg.

The random draws for the adverse-event grades use R's generator with a fixed
seed, so every regimen sees the same patients and the same uniform draws.

```{r regimens}
ladders <- list(
  "24 mg" = list(c(24, 20, 14, 10)),
  "20 mg" = list(c(20, 14, 10, 8)),
  "18 mg" = list(c(18, 14, 10, 8)),
  "14 mg" = list(c(14, 10, 8, 4)),
  "20 mg + up" = list(c(20, 14, 10, 8), c(24, 20, 14, 10)),
  "18 mg + up" = list(c(18, 14, 10, 8), c(24, 18, 14, 10)),
  "14 mg + up" = list(c(14, 10, 8, 4), c(20, 14, 10, 8), c(24, 20, 14, 10))
)

ladder_dose <- function(ladder, row, lev) {
  vapply(seq_along(row), function(i) ladder[[row[i]]][min(lev[i], 4L)], numeric(1))
}

simulate_regimen <- function(ladder, cohort, seed, n_weeks = 24) {
  set.seed(seed)
  n <- nrow(cohort)
  row <- rep(1L, n)
  lev <- rep(1L, n)
  n_red <- rep(0L, n)
  off <- rep(FALSE, n)
  withdrawn <- rep(FALSE, n)
  dose <- p_int <- p_red <- matrix(0, n, n_weeks)
  for (w in seq_len(n_weeks)) {
    if (length(ladder) > 1 && w > 1 && (w - 1) %% 4 == 0) {
      up <- !withdrawn & lev == 1L & n_red == 0L & row < length(ladder)
      row[up] <- row[up] + 1L
    }
    d <- ladder_dose(ladder, row, lev)
    d[withdrawn | off] <- 0
    dose[, w] <- d
    pr <- ae_probs(auc_len(d, cohort$cl, cohort$fcap), cohort$eta_ae)
    p_int[, w] <- pr$p1
    p_red[, w] <- pr$p2
    u <- runif(n)
    grade <- ifelse(u < pr$p0, 0L, ifelse(u < pr$p0 + pr$p1, 1L, 2L))
    on_drug <- d > 0
    reduce <- grade == 2L & on_drug
    off <- grade == 1L & on_drug
    n_red[reduce] <- n_red[reduce] + 1L
    lev[reduce] <- lev[reduce] + 1L
    withdrawn <- withdrawn | lev > 4L
  }
  list(dose = dose, n_red = n_red, p_int = p_int, p_red = p_red)
}

sims <- lapply(ladders, simulate_regimen, cohort = cohort, seed = 101)
```

## Table 3: average dose and dose reductions

```{r table3}
table3_paper <- data.frame(
  regimen = names(ladders),
  avg_paper = c(19.23, 16.09, 15.13, 12.15, 18.35, 17.90, 16.90),
  red1_paper = c(68.5, 60.8, 57.3, 46.9, 67.7, 67.7, 65.4),
  red2_paper = c(33.8, 22.3, 20.8, 12.3, 30.4, 28.1, 23.8)
)
table3_sim <- data.frame(
  regimen = names(sims),
  avg_sim = vapply(sims, function(s) mean(s$dose), numeric(1)),
  red1_sim = vapply(sims, function(s) 100 * mean(s$n_red >= 1), numeric(1)),
  red2_sim = vapply(sims, function(s) 100 * mean(s$n_red >= 2), numeric(1))
)
table3 <- left_join(table3_paper, table3_sim, by = "regimen")
table3 |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen,
    "Average dose, paper (mg/day)" = avg_paper,
    "Average dose, simulated (mg/day)" = avg_sim,
    ">= 1 reduction, paper (%)" = red1_paper,
    ">= 1 reduction, simulated (%)" = red1_sim,
    ">= 2 reductions, paper (%)" = red2_paper,
    ">= 2 reductions, simulated (%)" = red2_sim
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Replicates Table 3 of Hayato 2018 (200 simulated patients per regimen).")

stopifnot(
  # The average dose integrates every week's draw; a wrong EC50 unit or a
  # mis-signed threshold moves it by several mg/day.
  max(abs(table3$avg_sim / table3$avg_paper - 1)) < 0.05,
  max(abs(table3$red1_sim - table3$red1_paper)) < 8
)
```

The average dose and the share of patients with at least one reduction match
Table 3 closely for all seven regimens. The share with two or more reductions is
higher in this simulation than in the paper (for example 43% against 33.8% at
24 mg); it depends on the unpublished interruption and re-challenge rules, which
the share with one or more reductions does not.

## Figure 2 time course

```{r fig2}
sims[["24 mg"]][c("p_int", "p_red")] |>
  lapply(colMeans) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(week = seq_len(24)) |>
  pivot_longer(c(p_int, p_red), names_to = "panel", values_to = "prob") |>
  mutate(panel = recode(panel,
    p_int = "(a) AE leading to dose interruption",
    p_red = "(b) AE leading to dose reduction or withdrawal")) |>
  ggplot(aes(week, prob)) +
  geom_line(colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~panel) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 0.3)) +
  labs(x = "Time (weeks)", y = "Mean weekly probability",
       title = "Simulated 24 mg regimen (cf. Figure 2 of Hayato 2018)")
```

As in Figure 2, the probabilities peak in the first weeks and drift down as
dose reductions accumulate.

## Figure 3 and objective response

The tumor model is driven by the AUC of the average dose over each 8-week
interval between tumor assessments (weeks 0-8, 8-16 and 16-24).

```{r tumor-regimens}
tumor_events <- function(sim, cohort) {
  avg <- cbind(rowMeans(sim$dose[, 1:8]), rowMeans(sim$dose[, 9:16]),
               rowMeans(sim$dose[, 17:24]))
  auc <- auc_len(avg, cohort$cl, cohort$fcap)
  data.frame(
    id = rep(cohort$sid, each = 4),
    time = rep(c(0, 8, 16, 24), times = nrow(cohort)),
    evid = 0, cmt = "tumor", TUM_SLD = 60,
    AUC_LEN = as.vector(t(cbind(auc, auc[, 3])))
  )
}

tumor_sims <- lapply(names(sims), function(reg) {
  rxode2::rxSetSeed(2018)
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_tumor, tumor_events(sims[[reg]], cohort),
                  returnType = "data.frame") |>
    mutate(regimen = reg, rel = 100 * tumor / 60)
}) |>
  bind_rows()

fig3_paper <- data.frame(
  regimen = rep(c("24 mg", "20 mg", "18 mg", "14 mg", "20 mg + up", "18 mg + up", "14 mg + up"), each = 3),
  time = rep(c(8, 16, 24), times = 7),
  rel_paper = c(78.5, 69.7, 66.0, 80.2, 72.4, 68.7, 81.0, 73.4, 69.8, 83.3, 76.5, 73.6,
                79.5, 71.0, 67.0, 79.8, 71.3, 67.3, 81.7, 73.0, 68.9)
)
fig3_sim <- tumor_sims |>
  group_by(regimen, time) |>
  summarise(rel_sim = median(rel), .groups = "drop")
fig3 <- inner_join(fig3_paper, fig3_sim, by = c("regimen", "time"))

fig3_sim |>
  mutate(panel = ifelse(grepl("up", regimen) | regimen == "24 mg",
                        "(b) with up-titration", "(a) without up-titration")) |>
  bind_rows(filter(fig3_sim, regimen == "24 mg") |>
              mutate(panel = "(a) without up-titration")) |>
  distinct() |>
  ggplot(aes(time, rel_sim, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig3 |>
               mutate(panel = ifelse(grepl("up", regimen) | regimen == "24 mg",
                                     "(b) with up-titration", "(a) without up-titration")),
             aes(y = rel_paper), shape = 4) +
  facet_wrap(~panel) +
  labs(x = "Time (weeks)", y = "Median relative tumor size (%)",
       title = "Replicates Figure 3 of Hayato 2018 (lines: simulated; crosses: read from the figure)")

# Largest gap between the simulated and the published medians (percentage points).
round(max(abs(fig3$rel_sim - fig3$rel_paper)), 1)
stopifnot(
  # The median of 200 patients is a robust centre; the figure was read to
  # about 0.5 percentage points.
  max(abs(fig3$rel_sim - fig3$rel_paper)) < 5
)
```

The objective response rate (ORR) is the share of patients whose tumor is at
least 30% below baseline at a tumor assessment (weeks 8, 16 or 24), computed on
the individual predictions.

```{r orr}
orr <- tumor_sims |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(regimen, id) |>
  summarise(best = min(rel),
            confirmed = any(rel[time == 8] <= 70 & rel[time == 16] <= 70) |
              any(rel[time == 16] <= 70 & rel[time == 24] <= 70),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(orr_sim = 100 * mean(best <= 70),
            orr_confirmed = 100 * mean(confirmed), .groups = "drop")
orr_paper <- data.frame(
  regimen = names(ladders),
  orr_paper = c(50.0, 43.5, 41.5, 30.2, 46.8, 46.0, 41.7)
)
orr_tab <- left_join(orr_paper, orr, by = "regimen")
orr_tab |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen,
    "ORR at 24 weeks, paper (%)" = orr_paper,
    "ORR, simulated (%)" = orr_sim,
    "ORR with a confirming assessment, simulated (%)" = orr_confirmed
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "ORR at 24 weeks, Hayato 2018 Results text against simulation.")

stopifnot(
  # Structural: the approved 24 mg regimen gives the highest response and
  # 14 mg without up-titration the lowest, as in the paper.
  orr_tab$orr_sim[orr_tab$regimen == "24 mg"] > orr_tab$orr_sim[orr_tab$regimen == "14 mg"]
)
```

The simulated ORR runs 5 to 12 percentage points above the paper's values,
while the median tumor-size curves of Figure 3 agree to within 2.5 points. ORR is a threshold count in the tail of the distribution, so it is more
sensitive than the median to details the paper does not state: whether a
response needed confirmation (requiring it brings the simulation within about
five points of the paper), whether residual error was added to the simulated
profiles, the reading of the EC50 variability as a CV, and the patients' real
exposure distribution. As in the paper, 24 mg gives the highest response and
14 mg without up-titration the lowest; the ranking of the regimens in between
differs by a few points.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **No PK layer.** Exposure comes from the Gupta 2016 model
  (`Gupta_2016_lenvatinib`) at its reference covariates (75 kg, normal albumin
  and alkaline phosphatase, no interacting co-medication, capsule) with its
  between-subject variability on `CL/F` and `F`. The SELECT covariate
  distribution is not published in Hayato 2018.
* **Exposure units.** Hayato 2018 reports AUC and both EC50s in ug*h/mL. The
  models carry the package's canonical `AUC_LEN` in ng*h/mL and store the
  EC50s multiplied by 1000 (2030 and 2950 ng*h/mL).
* **EC50 variability of the tumor model.** Table 1 gives "CV %" = 40.5 for an
  exponential random effect. It is read as `sqrt(omega^2)`, the convention of
  the PDxPop software the authors used and of the same sponsor's later Majid
  2024 lenvatinib tumor model, giving `omega^2 = 0.164`; the alternative
  `log(1 + CV^2)` reading gives 0.152.
* **Residual error of the tumor model.** The paper states a combined additive
  and proportional error without saying how the parts combine. The model uses
  `combined1()` (standard deviations added), the form in the deposited code of
  the Majid 2024 successor model.
* **Tumor initial condition.** Table 1 has no baseline parameter, so the
  initial condition is the observed baseline sum of diameters (`TUM_SLD`). The
  vignette uses 60 mm for every patient; because the ODE is first order in tumor
  size, relative change does not depend on it.
* **Adverse-event model sign convention.** The paper models the logits of
  `P(grade >= i)`, so its threshold increment `B2 - B1 = -0.830` is negative.
  The model keeps that orientation rather than converting to the
  `P(grade <= m)` form used elsewhere in the package.
* **Dose-history rules.** The interruption length (one week), the
  re-challenge at the same dose after an interruption, withdrawal after the
  fourth level, and the up-titration rule (only from the first level of the
  current ladder and only before any reduction) are the maintainers' reading of
  the Methods and Online Resource Table 2; the paper does not spell them out.
  They reproduce Table 3's average dose and the share with one or more
  reductions, but give more patients with two or more reductions than Table 3.
* **ORR definition.** Response is a 30% decrease at week 8, 16 or 24 on the
  individual predictions, without confirmation, as the Methods describe it.
* **Figure 1.** The visual predictive check needs the SELECT data; the
  vignette shows the simulated intervals only.
* **Figure readings.** The Figure 2 week-1 values and the Figure 3 medians
  were read from the published figures by the maintainers.

## Errata

No erratum or correction to Hayato 2018 was found (Europe PMC, checked
2026-11-25).
